findings.where: every note edge against the desk; measured over the whole frame
findings.what: Nothing on this screen casts a contact shadow: building the paper mask (luminance>170, closed and filled), taking the Euclidean distance to it and excluding the near-black tear ink (luminance<65), the median desk luminance is 99.3 at 2-5px below a note, 95.7 at 5-10px, 96.3 at 10-20px and 99.3 at 60-120px, and above/left/right run 96.3-102.7 over the same bands - a spread of 3.6 levels out of ~98 (3.7%) with no direction and no falloff.
findings.why: The rubric requires contact shadows baked from the render's own lighting; here there is not even a uniform blur, so the notes are cut out and pasted onto the desk rather than resting on it.

findings.what: Its shadow is an opaque near-black quadrilateral, mean RGB (32,27,22) against a desk at luminance ~104, with a hard edge: at row 1370 the boundary goes 152 -> 32 in one pixel, at row 1263 it goes 19 -> 46 -> 90 -> 102 in three; and it protrudes both above-right (row 1263, x to 1397) and below-left (row 1380, x 1230-1288), so it is larger than the card in opposing directions.
findings.why: A shadow that is 70% darker than the desk, has a one-pixel edge and falls on two opposite sides at once is a black plane left in the render, not a contact shadow baked from any lighting.

findings.where: the opening note, frames 56-255 (app time 0.90s-4.08s; frames.json step_ms 16, playback_over_app_time 1.0)
findings.what: The note is a plain rectangle that only changes height: its left edge sits at x=61 and its right edge at x=773 in every sampled frame from 56 to 255 - width exactly 712px with zero variation - while height goes 160 -> 475px, and all four edges are machine-straight with sharp corners and no tear. The crease is equally flat: at frame 255 the trough row varies by sigma=1.33px (range 12px) across the full 712px width.
findings.why: The rubric asks for Blender-rendered folds and creases; a constant silhouette with a one-dimensional tonal band reads as a flat image being scaled, not as geometry catching light.

findings.where: the whole crop, box [928,254,1348,514] per logs/crops.json
findings.what: The crop named 'hand', which is the 300% view the rubric says handwriting is judged in, contains no handwriting at all: its left half is blank ruled paper and its right half is the 'Q search' chip set in the UI sans.
findings.why: The rubric judges handwriting at three hundred percent on the Chat hero, and the evidence offered for that judgement does not contain a handwritten glyph.

findings.where: the handwriting in the notes at 536-1007 and 1770-2295
findings.what: The hand is monoline with no pressure signature: within one line, mid-stroke width (skeleton pixels with exactly two neighbours, 2x distance transform) is p10 4.0, p50 6.0, p90 8.0 device px on 'You are the only thing' and p10 4.0, p50 6.0, p90 8.0 on 'Rain. The first in a', and at 10x nearest-neighbour zoom the entries and exits of every stroke are the same weight as its middle. logs/hand.json's own numbers agree that glyphs repeat: 45 of 491 marks (9.2%) have a near-twin at IoU 0.85, and best_fit_iou max is 1.0, i.e. at least one pair of marks is identical once normalised.
findings.why: The rubric asks for multiple variants per glyph and real pressure variance; constant stroke weight plus an exactly repeated mark is a font, not a hand.

findings.where: the search chip (x 1130-1416, y 289-380) and the five tab slabs (y 2960-3100)
findings.what: The chrome is flat rectangles with a uniform drop shadow, not paper: the chip's left edge deviates by sigma=0.76px (range 4px) over 80 rows and its top edge by sigma=1.42px, and the CHAT tab's top edge by sigma=0.32px (range 1px) over 250px of width, over a flat near-white fill.
findings.why: Rectangles with machine-cut edges and a soft uniform blur under them are the simulated-card surface the anti-goal names, and they sit in the same frame as the torn notes.

findings.where: the desk in the gap between the note ending at y=475 and the note starting at y=536
findings.what: Ruled lines are painted outside the paper onto the wood: a one-pixel-tall bright line at y=485 runs x=683-990 (307px) where luminance jumps from ~100 to ~163 and back within a single row, with a shorter one at y=485 x=313-365 and a third at y=2674 x=234-309, plus a fainter dashed row at y=506-509.
findings.why: Paper ruling drawn on the desk is a mask that does not hold, and it shows in the same 300% crop (crops/02_chat_300_shadow.png) the rubric sends a critic to.

findings.where: the bottom tear of every note, e.g. y 930-1020 and y 2230-2310
findings.what: The tear fringe reads as ink rather than fibre: the darkest strands average RGB (44,37,31), 55-60% darker than the desk at ~104, and 37% of pixels four device px below the paper edge are under luminance 65, with strands running up to 20px onto the wood before the desk returns to baseline.
findings.why: Torn paper fibre is lighter than the sheet and casts a thin shadow; a near-black spiky rim reads as a brush stroke around a cut-out.

findings.what: Fourteen of the fifteen artifacts present are stale - only 02_chat.png carries from_this_run true - and every clip, including 06_unfolding.mp4 which the rubric names for slow-motion judgement, was written before this capture began at 18:13:19Z; 09_two_devices.png and 16_setup_android.png are absent with the reason 'not captured this session'.
findings.why: The rubric's two named judgements are the Chat hero and the unfolding clip, and the unfolding clip is not evidence of what the build currently renders.

what_is_working: Tear masks do not repeat on a single screen. Detrending the top and bottom edge profiles of all seven paper elements in 02_chat.png and cross-correlating each pair, the largest normalised match is 0.305 (note A bottom against the voice note top); no pair exceeds 0.31. logs/tears.json's own count of 8 distinct tears across 8 notes from a pool of 56 is consistent with what the picture shows.

No tiled texture in the paper. The 2-D autocorrelation of the high-passed interior of the Rain note (490x990px, ink clipped out) has no off-origin lattice peak; the largest is 0.30 at |dx| ~ 19px, which is the correlation length of the mottle rather than a repeat. Blank 60x60px patches inside four different notes give high-pass sigma of 1.05-2.40 levels with no shared phase.
01_pulse.png's torn edges hold up at 1:1: fine white fibre reads against the dark desk on the two large notes, and the desk itself carries knots and curved grain rather than a comb of stripes.

Feelings are physical objects, not icons, and the landing object is real geometry: in 07_feeling_landing.mp4 at frame 110 the peg casts a shadow down-right onto the drum face and the drum casts a soft shadow right onto the paper, one light from upper-left.

The crease shading in 06_unfolding.mp4 is directionally consistent: at frame 255 both creases show a highlight above (row mean peaking at 244.0) and a trough below (229.5), and per-column crease contrast varies 10-23 levels rather than being a constant step.

Two visibly distinct hands share the Chat hero - the slanted one on 'told you. august' and 'its raining here too', the upright one on 'You are the only thing' and 'Rain. The first in a month' - so the two people do not write with the same pen.
Every clip is honestly assembled: frames.json reports 0 repeated frames, longest_still_run 0 and 0 brightness jumps for all five clips, at playback_over_app_time 1.0.
verdict: The paper itself is the strongest part of this build and it is genuinely good: the tear masks are all different on one screen (max cross-correlation between any two edge profiles 0.305), the stock carries a mottle with no tile in it, and the feeling objects are rendered geometry with their own lit shadows rather than icons. What fails is everything that makes paper sit in a place. Once the near-black tear ink is excluded, the desk in 02_chat.png is the same brightness two pixels from a note as it is a hundred and twenty pixels away - 95.7 to 102.7 across every band and every direction - so not one note casts a contact shadow, and in 01_pulse.png the 'goodnight' card's shadow is an opaque quadrilateral at RGB (32,27,22) with a one-pixel edge that protrudes on two opposite sides at once, which is a black plane in the render rather than light. The unfolding clip, which the rubric sends a critic to in slow motion, is a rectangle whose width is exactly 712px in every frame from 56 to 255 while its height triples: a flat sheet being scaled, with a crease whose trough sits within 1.33px of the same row across the whole width. The hand is monoline with no entry or exit thinning, hand.json's own measurement finds one pair of marks identical after normalisation and 9.2% with near-twins, and the 300% crop supplied for judging the hand contains no handwriting at all. Add the ruled lines painted 307px across the bare desk at y=485 and the flat machine-cut chip and tab slabs whose edges hold to sigma under a pixel, and the screen reads as very well-made cut-outs arranged on a photograph rather than as objects lying on a desk. Three of the six things this row names - contact shadows, rendered folds, pressure variance - are not there, so it sits below its floor.
